column1: # The red run: this tree's assertions against the engine the base ref holds,
# written whole by tests/red, which tests/run --record-assertions calls.
#   base  <ref>  <sha>  <engine version there>
#   run   <failed>  <passed>  <skipped>        lines counted, not the summary
#   <assertion name>  <times it failed>        failed names only
# A base of - means no red run was possible. Reproduce with: tests/red <ref>
base
run
and so when its errors go to /dev/null: the 2 of 2>/dev/null is no second ref
and the row's reason is given
blind allow case 26: update-ref writes refs/heads/backup, and the remote-tracking ref is only the value it reads
blind allow case 27: symbolic-ref with one ref reads it and prints
the founder's case 10: a here-document a shell reads is its script
the founder's case 11: and so with -s
the founder's case 12: a redirect's target is written whatever line the here-document ends on
the founder's case 1: a separator glued to the last word ends it, as the shell does
the founder's case 2: a group's separator ends the word too
the founder's case 3: a line break ends a word as a blank does
the founder's case 4: a shell's -c script is a command of its own, quotes and all
the founder's case 5: and so under bash -c
the founder's case 6: a -c script handed to find's -exec is still a command
the founder's case 7: a $( ) assigned to a variable runs
the founder's case 8: a quoted program name is the program
the founder's case 9: a quoted path in command position runs
the reader prints a command separator as a token of its own, an operator of two characters whole
the target of a redirect after that read is a file, not a second ref
